answer: An Ivory-island public-table bond stops bulk fakes. Each identity locks 70 credits and files one row in a public ivory table: its island plot, a fresh serial, and a falcon-stamped survey. Auditors recheck one plot in ten; a reused serial, a wrong island, or a copied falcon stamp burns the bond. A filing costs 40 credits, rising 6 each, so the thousandth pays 6,034. Forging 1,000 fakes costs 3,037,000 for a 40,000 pool. Honest agents file once.
